start: ^Narrator: A man in his late twenties sits at a workstation, headphones on, three terminals of log output scrolling past. He notices you and pulls the headphones down.
^Owen Gallagher: Hey. You're the security consultant? Owen Gallagher, sysadmin.
^Owen Gallagher: Finally, someone who might actually fix our mess.
^What can you tell me about the breach?
^I'll need your help with technical access.
^Point me at the logs. I'll take it from here.

c-0: ^You: What can you tell me about the data leaving the building?
c-1: ^You: I'll need your help with access. Server logs, badges, that kind of thing.
^Owen Gallagher: Sure. Whatever you need, within reason.
c-2: ^You: Just point me at the logs. I'll take it from here.
^Owen Gallagher: Right. Terminal's over there. Shout if you need anything.

network_situation: ^Owen Gallagher: Someone's been pushing huge files out between two and four in the morning.
^Owen Gallagher: I thought it was remote work at first. But the pattern's too tidy. Same hours, same encrypted channel, same research share.

c-0: ^You: Why didn't you report it earlier?
^Owen Gallagher: I did. Patricia's been on it for three weeks. Then someone upstairs told her to leave it.

hub: ^(Lean over his log screen, close enough for the cloner to reach his lanyard.)

c-7: ^You: That's everything for now. Catch you later.
^Owen Gallagher: Cool. I'll be here. I'm always here.

ask_network: ^Owen Gallagher: Standard setup. Corporate VPN, segmented VLANs. The research portal sits on its own subnet behind the server room.
^Owen Gallagher: Server hallway's badge-only. The server room itself has a password on the door, which I'm told is "temporary". It's been temporary for a year.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: There's a terminal in there that can see the research subnet. If you want to know what's on the portal, start there.

ask_torres: ^Owen Gallagher: David? Scarily smart. Doctorate in cryptography.
^Owen Gallagher: Works late a lot. Always stressed. His wife's ill, so... yeah.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: I saw him in the server hallway the other night. Not doing anything. Just standing there, looking wrecked.

ask_security: ^Owen Gallagher: Security's not great. Budget cuts. We log access, but nobody watches it live.
^Owen Gallagher: And the physical locks are the cheap pin-tumbler kind. I proved that on last year's pen test.
owen_clone: ^Narrator: You lean in while he scrolls the logs.

b: ^Narrator: The cloner buzzes once against your hip.
^Owen Gallagher: Did your bag just beep? ...You read my badge. Fair. I did half of Finance on last year's pen test.
^Narrator: The cloner didn't get a clean read.

c-0: ^Owen Gallagher: Don't be. Just don't let Patricia see you do it.
c-1: ^Owen Gallagher: Yeah. That's what I told Finance.

request_password: ^You: The server room wants a password.
^Owen Gallagher: After-hours server access gets logged with IT. That's me.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: Patricia signed off David's office, not the server room. Get her to put her name to that too, or give me a reason I can write in the log.
^Owen Gallagher: Give me a reason I can write in the log. Or get Patricia to put her name to it.

request_password: ^Patricia's log has a crypto badge in your server room at 23:47, and nobody logged it with you.
^Security's signed it off. Check your messages.

c-0: ^You: Patricia's log has a crypto badge in your server room at 23:47, and nobody logged it with you.
^Owen Gallagher: ...Nobody logged that with me. Right.
c-1: ^You: Security's signed it off. Check your messages.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: There's a message from Security. Not from Patricia's phone, though. ...Fine.
^Owen Gallagher: Yeah, she has. "On my authority." She does like that phrase.

password_given: ^Owen Gallagher: It's on my monitor. It's been on my monitor for a year. Take it, and please don't put that in your report.
^Owen Gallagher: Past the server room is the key vault. Fingerprint reader. David's thumb and nobody else's. Don't ask me how you'd get in there.
request_office_card: ^You: I need to get into David Torres' office.

b: ^Owen Gallagher: I got a message from Security saying you can have the spares. Nobody's answering down there, though. Is Patricia all right?
^Owen Gallagher: Here. IT's spare. I hope you don't find anything.
^Owen Gallagher: Yeah, Patricia messaged. On her authority, she said. Twice.
^Owen Gallagher: IT's spare. I hope you don't find anything.
^Owen Gallagher: ...Fine. That's IT's spare. I didn't give it to you.
^Owen Gallagher: I hope you don't find anything in there.

request_office_card: ^Owen Gallagher: David's office? No chance. Not without Patricia signing it off.
^Owen Gallagher: I like my job. Get her to message me and it's yours.
owen_told: ^Owen Gallagher: David? No way. He wouldn't...
^Owen Gallagher: He stood in the hallway looking wrecked and I just... walked past him.
^Keep it to yourself until it's done.

c-0: ^You: You couldn't have known. That's how they work.
^Owen Gallagher: Yeah. Doesn't help much, but thanks.
c-1: ^You: Keep this to yourself until it's over.
^Owen Gallagher: Who would I even tell?
